units.title: Acute Gout: Aim and Drugs
units.sec: Acute Gout: Aim and Drugs · p242
units.guide: Acute gout aims to decrease inflammation and give symptomatic relief — not to lower uric acid yet. NSAIDs first; if no response, a steroid. DOC is indomethacin (multiple MOAs). Colchicine inhibits microtubules → chemotaxis/migration of leucocytes, ↓IL-1 from neutrophils, and phagocytosis. S/E: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, marrow suppression, alopecia.

units.title: Chronic Gout: Aim and Classification
units.sec: Chronic Gout: Aim and Classification · p242
units.guide: Chronic gout aims to prevent acute attacks by lowering uric acid: inhibit synthesis (XO inhibitors), increase excretion (uricosurics), or increase metabolism (uricase analogs).

units.title: Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors: Allopurinol
units.guide: Allopurinol is DOC for chronic gout, tumor lysis, Lesch-Nyhan and organ transplant. Hypersensitivity m/c = SJS (HLA-B*5801); also orotidylate decarboxylase block → orotic aciduria, and DRESS. Class: xanthinuria → xanthine stones; acute gout flare prevented with NSAID/colchicine 3–6 months. Interaction: ↑ 6-MP / azathioprine toxicity.

units.title: Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors: Oxypurinol and Febuxostat
units.sec: Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors: Oxypurinol and Febuxostat · p243
units.guide: Oxypurinol is an orphan drug for allopurinol hypersensitivity. Febuxostat is for intolerance or inadequate response; S/E increased cardiovascular death.

units.title: Uricosuric Drugs
units.guide: Probenecid and sulfinpyrazone: add-on > monotherapy. Benzbromarone and lesinurad: most effective, add-on only, usable in mild–moderate renal failure. S/E: urate stones (C/I previous stones), calcium stones, precipitate acute gout. Comorbid add-ons: losartan (HTN), atorvastatin (↑LDL), fenofibrate (↑TG).

units.title: Uricase Analogues
units.guide: Humans have no uricase. Pegloticase: resistant gout, IV every 2 weeks. Rasburicase: DOC high-risk tumor lysis (leukemia, especially CLL). S/E: hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and methemoglobinemia.
